supersedes.reason: independent audit 6 of release-v6 (evidence/release-designs-t076-2026-09-25.md): Y1 judge shopping: verify_trial could be called repeatedly on one journalled trial, re-asking the judge each time, and verify_suite took one result per slot without reading the judge log, so a trial judged not_supported could be re-verified until supported and reach scoped_pass; Y2 the request-id anchor was defeatable by reuse and the audit was one-directional: no code required distinct ids, a scripted critic wrapped in hand-built ProviderReply objects with one request id for every call passed, and an id of any form ('x') was accepted. Non-blocking items 2 to 6 are fixed or stated here. release-v1..v6 are kept unchanged.

purpose: The release qualification design for the Q01-family critic configuration: a scoped acceptance rule for one exact critic configuration on one sealed set, frozen before any heldout material exists. A pass is a scoped pass and never a qualification: this design has no generation path and cannot verify V3 error independence.
execution_state: kept outside this pinned file in a run record whose pre-dispatch part is frozen by sha256 before the first dispatch (see pre_dispatch)

critic_configuration.digest: critic_configuration_digest = sha256 of the canonical JSON (sorted keys, separators (',', ':'), ensure_ascii False, allow_nan False, UTF-8) of exactly these fields; a scoped pass is bound to this digest, and the product computes the same digest for a deployed critic
critic_configuration.call_and_run_deadlines: an object with both call_seconds and run_seconds (required)
critic_configuration.critic_prompt_digest: sha256 of the canonical JSON {instruction.md, app/services/design_criticism_live.py, app/generation_profiles.py: file sha256}, i.e. every source of each call's system prompt (q01_harness.critic_prompt_digest)
critic_configuration.lens_refs_and_digests: {pack_id, pack_version, pack_sha256, rules: [{lens_id, version, sha256}]} of the lens pack sent at every counterexample-proposal call (canonical sha256 of the pack and of each rule, equal to the product's prepared-input manifest). The lens pack is critic configuration: it is supplied to the harness with the configuration, never read from the sealed bundle, and a sealed case that carries a lens pack is refused by the harness and the verifier. A configuration with no lens set uses a pack with no rules.
critic_configuration.checked_at_dispatch: Before any read the harness checks contract_version, parser_version, critic_prompt_digest, max_proposed_chains, call_seconds, run_seconds, lens_refs_and_digests and the declared critic transport (run_identity.critic_transport) against the running configuration. At every call it checks provider, mode, model and effort against the call's frozen selection (what the call was ASKED to use) and the lens pack digests at every proposal call. After every completed call it checks what SERVED the call: the served model, the provider request id and the provider message id that the provider's response reported (the product Claude adapter parses the response message's model and id and the request-id header; the rig's attested turn returns them in an app.critic_trial.ProviderReply), which the runner binds into the call's durable ledger details. A call without a provider-reported served model, without a request id in the adapter's exact form req_[A-Za-z0-9]{8,128}, without a message id in the provider's form msg_[A-Za-z0-9_]{8,196} (the message id is required), or whose served model is not exactly critic_configuration.model, ends the trial as invalid (transport_identity_unattested). The verifier re-derives the selection and the provider-reported identity from each call's durable ledger details and makes the trial invalid on either mismatch, even when the harness check was bypassed; it also makes a trial invalid when any provider id repeats within it (provider_id_reused), and verify_suite requires every id distinct across the suite. The exact model string is compared: a configuration must pin the exact model string the provider reports (an alias resolving to a snapshot is a mismatch). max_tokens is not observable by the transport and is recorded as unchecked in each trial record. The verifier also requires the recorded proposed_not_driven to equal max(0, number of proposed counterexamples - max_proposed_chains).
critic_configuration.lens_arm: The configuration names its lens set explicitly (possibly empty); a pass never carries over between a lens and a no-lens configuration.
critic_configuration.transport: A release trial must run through the provider-attested transport: the Claude rig's attested_turn over the product ClaudeAPIAdapter with no injected transport (claude_rig transport=None; run_identity.critic_transport = {injected: false, name: null}). No named test double is allowed for release: the manifest check refuses an injected transport for a release-v7 run, the harness refuses dispatch when the turn's declared transport differs from the manifest, and the verifier refuses a trial whose recorded transport, or the transport digest bound in its frozen calls, differs. A scripted (system, user) -> str callable is the calibration and development transport: its calls carry model identity selection_declared_not_transport_reported and can never complete a release trial. Code checks the declared path, the reported model and the form and distinctness of the ids; it cannot tell a reply the adapter parsed from a real provider response from one constructed in-process or served by a fake server (see open): that is caught only by the two-way reconciliation with the provider's records (acceptance.post_verdict_audit).

run_identity.rule: Run identity describes one attempt and is never part of the critic configuration; every field is fixed in the pre-dispatch manifest. Every verifier result binds to the manifest sha256, the critic configuration digest, the judge identity and prompt digest of this run identity and its journalled slot; a result that does not is not part of the suite.
run_identity.planned_slots: the planned (case, repetition) slot list: case_order x 3, case-major and in order [(order[0],1),(order[0],2),(order[0],3),(order[1],1),...], fixed before the first dispatch; the dispatch journal must follow it
run_identity.trial_base_dir: the only directory under which the harness creates this manifest's trial directories (audit 5, non-blocking 1): the harness refuses a release trial with any other base directory, and verify_suite scans the directory and requires every dispatched trial record naming this manifest (one carrying a journal entry, a call or a read) to be in the dispatch journal with that entry. Restoring an earlier copy of the journal after a failed trial therefore leaves that trial's directory as evidence and the suite incomplete.
run_identity.sealed_case_sha256s: case id -> sha256 of that case file, exactly the entries of the sealed environment manifest (checked by the harness against the environment it reads and by the verifier against the sealed bundle); every case id and case sha256 is compared with the prior attempts' (pre_dispatch.spent_sets)
run_identity.judge_model: the exact model the judge provider must report serving for every judged semantic item; null when no provider judge is configured (semantic items are then not_judged under this design)
run_identity.critic_transport: {injected, name}: whether a custom transport was injected into the Claude rig (audit 6, non-blocking 5). A release run must name the product adapter path {injected: false, name: null}; an injected transport is invalid for release because this design names no test double. It is recorded in the manifest, in every trial record and, as a digest, in every frozen call's code hashes.

pre_dispatch.content: the critic configuration and its digest, the full run identity (including planned_slots, the dispatch journal path, the trial base directory, the judge model, every sealed case's sha256 and the critic transport path), the attempt number and every prior attempt for this critic configuration digest with its design id, sealed dataset sha256, sealed expectations sha256, case ids, case sha256s and verdict, the author, reviewer and sealing attestations (name, statement, date; author and reviewer differ, the judge is none of author, reviewer and sealer, names compared case- and whitespace-normalized), and, when the lens-effect design runs, the lens_effect section of lens-effects-v7 (per-arm critic configurations and digests, per-arm attempt entries, the qualification sets the effect set must differ from, non-null text digests for general_multi_perspective and every lens arm, the arm x case order interleaved per case, predictions sha256)
pre_dispatch.freeze: The manifest's sha256 is committed to the repository (or recorded with an external timestamp) before the first dispatch; the commit id or the timestamp reference is given to the harness with every trial (PreDispatch.commit_ref) and recorded in the dispatch journal header, every trial record and the suite record. The harness refuses to dispatch unless the manifest it loads hashes to the committed value, its harness identity equals the running harness, and every observable critic-configuration field equals the running configuration; the suite record carries that sha256 and the verifier re-checks the full manifest (there is no hash-values-only path). That the commit or timestamp precedes the first ledger event is checked after the verdict (acceptance.post_verdict_audit).
pre_dispatch.harness: PreDispatch.harness (the expected harness identity), PreDispatch.lens_pack (the configuration's lens pack), PreDispatch.repetition (the trial's slot, with the case id) and PreDispatch.commit_ref are mandatory for every release trial. The product adapter (app/adapters/claude_api.py) is pinned only through this per-attempt harness identity: it is in the harness file set (q01_harness.HARNESS_FILES), the manifest's run_identity.harness fixes that file set's sha256, and the harness refuses dispatch when the running files differ. This design's FROZEN.json pins the evals code and the gate, never the product adapter (audit 6, non-blocking 6): a product adapter change needs a new pre-dispatch manifest, not a new design version.
pre_dispatch.edits: Any change after the freeze voids the attempt as incomplete; the sealed set is still spent.
pre_dispatch.spent_sets: The manifest check refuses a run whose sealed_dataset_sha256 or sealed_expectations_sha256 equals either sha of any listed prior attempt, and (audit 5, non-blocking 3) a run any of whose case ids (the published hash of each expectation case key, candidate id and counterexample id) or case sha256s appears among any listed prior attempt's case ids or case sha256s, so re-serializing the environment manifest or re-bundling spent cases does not make a spent set new; the same for each lens-effect arm's prior attempts; a lens-effect set equal to any listed qualification set is refused. The suite record carries every prior attempt's sealed set sha256 and a digest of the prior-attempt list, and the product gate refuses a record whose sealed set is among them. These comparisons catch exact reuse only (audit 6, non-blocking 2): a spent case that is edited (new bytes) and renamed (a new candidate or counterexample id, hence a new case id) passes them. Such re-use is excluded by dataset.must_be_new through the author's statement, the reviewer's check and the sealing attestation (human review, not code), and by the post-verdict audit item that no other known attempt or manifest used this set or any of its cases, paraphrased or not.

dispatch_journal.requirement: one append-only, hash-chained dispatch journal per manifest, at run_identity.dispatch_journal.path (owner-controlled, outside the repository)
dispatch_journal.format: JSON lines; each line is the canonical JSON of one entry. Entry 0 is the header {schema q01-dispatch-journal-2, seq 0, kind open, manifest_sha256, commit_ref, planned_slots_sha256, prev (64 zeros), entry_sha256}; every further entry is {seq, kind dispatch, trial_id, case_id, repetition, prev, entry_sha256}, except at most one final {seq, kind stop, reason, prev, entry_sha256}, after which no entry may follow; prev is the previous entry's entry_sha256 and entry_sha256 is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the entry without that key.
dispatch_journal.write: The harness writes a trial's id and its (case, repetition) slot, fixed in PreDispatch, before the trial's first read or call: under an exclusive lock it re-reads and chain-checks the journal, refuses a slot that is not the next planned slot (out of order, repeated, extra), appends with O_APPEND and fsyncs. The entry sha256 is recorded in the trial record and bound into every frozen call's code hashes in the durable ledger. No entry is ever rewritten or removed.
dispatch_journal.verify: verify_trial reads the repetition from the record's journalled slot and refuses a differing caller value; it requires the trial to be in the journal with that slot, entry sha256 and commit reference, and the entry to be bound in the ledger. verify_suite requires the set of results to equal the journal exactly (a journalled trial missing or not submitted, or a result not in the journal, is incomplete) and the journal to follow planned_slots in order (an out-of-order or extra slot is incomplete). The journal head goes into the suite record. A stop entry makes the suite incomplete, and every dispatched trial record of this manifest under run_identity.trial_base_dir must be in the journal (run_identity.trial_base_dir).
dispatch_journal.stop: The T077 dispatcher (the code that authorizes and sequences the trials of a manifest, not yet written) enforces usd_hard_stop: before a trial whose spend could cross it, or when it is crossed, it appends the stop entry through q01_harness.journal_stop. The harness refuses every dispatch after a stop. verify_suite reads the stop from the journal (audit 5, non-blocking 7): it takes no caller flag, and a stopped run is incomplete; the suite record carries run_stopped. Until that dispatcher exists and is pinned in a later version, no release run executes.

dataset.must_be_new: No case, material, candidate, counterexample or wording from evals/deeptwin/q01_materials.py, q01_lenses.json, the ten calibration cases, or ANY previously dispatched sealed set (qualification or lens-effect, any design version), nor paraphrases of them. The lens pack is critic configuration, not dataset material: the sealed bundle never carries it, and the materials are not written to suit a lens.

authoring.author: A named person who has not seen the verifier's calibration expectations and does not tune the critic configuration.
excluded_as_author_reviewer_or_judge: the developer who built the Q01 harness and verifiers
anyone who tuned the critic configuration
any model or session with repository access
authoring.expectations: Written by the author from the new materials alone as data conforming to sealed_expectation.schema.json (allowed statuses per criterion, evidence rules, validity and response expectations, judge items with rubrics), before any trial, and sealed (content sha256 in the pre-dispatch manifest).
authoring.judge_rubrics: Written by the author as part of the sealed expectations and checked by the reviewer; the judge never edits them.
authoring.task_package: The agent sees the Q01 instruction.md and a fixed-criteria document written by the author for the new materials; Task.md's M01/catalog-specific wording is replaced by the author's criteria text, frozen with the set.
authoring.review: A second named person, not the author and not the judge, checks each expectation and rubric against the materials before sealing; a disagreement is resolved or the case is dropped before sealing, never after.
authoring.attestations: The author, the reviewer and the sealing step each record an attestation (name, statement, date) in the pre-dispatch manifest.

required_coverage: at least one required_defect for each of Q1 (meaning), Q2 (hand-off), Q3 (authority)
at least one valid alternative candidate under Q4
at least one Q5 pair (a valid counterexample handled and one not handled)
composition.checked: The verifier checks every coverage rule decidable from the expectations when it loads them and records whether it did; a suite over expectations loaded without that check is incomplete. The Q4 alternative stays a reviewer check.
composition.exclusions: Only before the first dispatch, with the reason recorded; composition and coverage are re-checked after any exclusion. Nothing is excluded after the first dispatch: a disputed case then makes the suite incomplete.
composition.note: A scoped design choice so every class and criterion has instances; it is not a statistical sample size and supports no rate estimate.

storage_and_access.location: outside the git repository, in an owner-controlled location recorded by path and sha256 in the pre-dispatch manifest
storage_and_access.during_run: agent inputs come only from the harness's allowlisted reader; expectations are read only by the verifier at verify time; every read is logged in the run record
storage_and_access.results: the developer reads trial outputs and verdicts only after the suite verdict is recorded
storage_and_access.single_use: The first dispatched trial marks the set observed and spent forever (it becomes development data). Exactly one run per sealed set: no continuation, merge or rerun. Every trial dispatched under a manifest is in its dispatch journal and its directory under run_identity.trial_base_dir; a set, or any case, that a listed prior attempt used is refused by the manifest check.
storage_and_access.attempt_ledger: Every attempt for one critic configuration digest is numbered across sets and design versions; each pre-dispatch manifest lists all prior attempts with their sealed dataset and sealed expectations sha256, case ids, case sha256s and verdicts, and any claim cites 'attempt k' with every prior verdict. Nothing in code enumerates every manifest written for a configuration digest (see open).

verifier.requirement: A data-driven verifier, not evals/deeptwin/verifiers/critic.py (whose expectations are the calibration cases), that loads the sealed expectations only at verify time, derives material checks and leak markers from the sealed set, takes the lens pack only from the critic configuration, refuses a sealed case whose source or candidate carries a key outside the input contract, and implements the same outcome classes (pass, fail, not_judged, invalid) and the six boundary classes. It makes a trial invalid (transport_identity_unattested) when any call's durable details lack the provider-reported served model and request id or the served model is not the configured model, and accepts a semantic status only when it is re-derived from the judge provider's durable raw response with the judge provider's reported model (equal to run_identity.judge_model) and request id. It judges each trial at most once (audit 6, Y1): the trial's judge log (judge-responses.jsonl under run_identity.trial_base_dir/<trial id>) is created exclusively before the judge is asked anything, every answer and any judge fault is appended as it arrives, and a trial whose judge log already exists is invalid (trial_already_judged) without any judge call; verify_suite re-reads each trial's full judge log and requires it to be exactly the lines its result judged (by lines_sha256). It requires every critic request id and message id and every judge request id in the adapter's forms and distinct within the trial and across the suite (audit 6, Y2), and the trial's recorded critic transport to be the manifest's.
verifier.freeze: Its version and file-set sha256 are fixed in the pre-dispatch manifest before sealing; it is written by the harness developer without access to the sealed set and tested only on development data.

state_at_freeze.statement: The data-driven verifier exists at this freeze (evals/deeptwin/verifiers/sealed_critic.py); its identity is below and every file it covers is also pinned in FROZEN.json.

harness_at_freeze.statement: The harness identity (q01_harness.harness_identity) covers these files and app/adapters/claude_api.py. The product adapter's hash is deliberately not recorded here or in FROZEN.json: it is pinned per attempt only, by run_identity.harness in the pre-dispatch manifest, and the harness refuses dispatch when the running file set differs (audit 6, non-blocking 6). No harness file-set sha256 is recorded at the design freeze for the same reason.

verifier.results: Each trial result carries the trial id, its journalled slot and journal entry sha256, the trial record sha256, the ledger head, the manifest sha256, the critic configuration digest, the judge identity and prompt digest, and its own result_sha256; a suite accepts only results issued by verify_trial in the same process and unaltered, exactly the journalled trials, one per (case, repetition) slot. Each result also carries whether every critic call and every judged item was provider-reported (critic_transport_identity, judge_transport_identity) and the path and digest of the trial's durable judge log. Each result also carries the provider ids it relies on (critic request and message ids, judge request and message ids) and its judge log's path, line count and lines_sha256; the suite checks the ids' forms and distinctness and re-reads every judge log.

execution.repetitions_fixed: fixed by this design and by the verifier (REPETITIONS_PER_CASE = 3); never supplied by the caller; each trial's repetition is fixed in PreDispatch and journalled before dispatch, never assigned at verify time
execution.repetition_meaning: three calls on one case are one task sample, never three independent samples
execution.output_contract_error: a completed trial whose output breaks the contract is a fail of that repetition (Task.md), never an invalid trial
execution.invalid_trials: only harness, evidence, isolation, configuration, transport identity (transport_identity_unattested, provider_id_reused, critic_transport_differs_from_manifest) or judge failures (including trial_already_judged); reported with cause, never scored, never replaced within the run (a replacement is an extra slot the harness refuses and the verifier treats as incomplete)
execution.authority: The pre-dispatch manifest names who authorized the run, the authority reference and the budget; without it the run is not executed and there is no verdict
execution.spend: a hard USD stop (run_identity.usd_hard_stop) fixed before any call and enforced by the T077 dispatcher, which journals a stop entry (pre_dispatch.dispatch_journal.stop); a stopped run is incomplete, and the stop is read from the journal, never supplied by a caller
execution.order: trials are dispatched in run_identity.planned_slots order, one at a time; the harness refuses any other slot

judge.independence_profile: The profile in force is the one whose path and sha256 the pre-dispatch manifest records. independence_profile.json here fixes the rules (judge separation not established); a successor profile that records an established judge is frozen and committed before sealing, has schema q01-independence-profile-6, names this design id, and records the judge identity, prompt digest and option. The verifier loads the profile bytes, checks the sha256 and design id and derives judge separation from them; no caller flag exists.
judge.judge_binding: the profile's judge, run_identity.judge_identity and judge_prompt_digest, and every judged result's judge must be the same; an other_provider judge needs a non-null prompt digest; a judge identity or judge model that names the critic's provider family or model string is refused, using a provider/family alias table (for example anthropic: anthropic, claude, opus, sonnet, haiku; openai: openai, gpt, codex, chatgpt; google: google, gemini) with case-insensitive substring matching. This check only guards against accidental self-judging: it compares declared names and cannot detect a judge that hides its provider. The judge is none of the author, reviewer and sealer (case- and whitespace-normalized).
judge.judge_errors: every judge verdict is recorded beside the sealed expectation; a judge failure makes that trial invalid (Task.md Q8); judge-versus-expectation disagreements are listed, never folded into the critic's score
judge.judge_attestation: A semantic status counts only when the judge returns an attested answer (judge_attested): the judge provider's raw response, from which the verifier re-derives the verdict, with the served model and the request id (in the adapter's req_ form; a message id, when reported, in the safe-id form) the judge provider's response reported; the served model must equal run_identity.judge_model exactly (else the trial is invalid, judge_identity_mismatch). The verifier appends every answer as received, with its reported identity, to the trial's durable judge log (judge-responses.jsonl, O_APPEND and fsync) before checking it. A judge that only declares its identity and prompt digest, an answer without a reported model or such a request id, or a run without a judge_model leaves the item not_judged (never pass). No provider reports a human reviewer's identity: under this design a human reviewer's answers leave the items not_judged (see open).
judge.one_judging_per_trial: Exactly one judging per trial (audit 6, Y1). The judge log is created with O_EXCL at the start of judging, with an opening line naming the trial, the judge and the items; a trial whose judge log already exists is refused (trial_already_judged) without asking the judge, whatever judge is supplied. verify_suite re-reads each submitted trial's judge log: a result that judged must match the full log exactly (lines_sha256 and line count), a result that judged nothing requires that no judge log exist, and any extra judging, edited or removed log is incomplete. The suite record carries each trial's judge-log digest. A judge wrapper that re-asks its provider and returns the best answer is not visible to code: every judge-model request of the run window must be a logged request id (acceptance.post_verdict_audit).

acceptance.case_pass: a case passes only if every one of its 3 repetitions is a distinct valid trial that passes under the frozen data-driven verifier

suite_outcome.fail: any valid repetition failed; takes precedence over invalid, not_judged and incomplete
suite_outcome.incomplete: no fail, and any of: an invalid (including transport_identity_unattested, provider_id_reused, critic_transport_differs_from_manifest and trial_already_judged), missing, duplicated or stopped repetition; a stop entry in the dispatch journal; a result not issued by verify_trial or altered; one trial used for more than one slot; a result of another manifest, configuration or judge; a result whose trial is not in the manifest's dispatch journal with that slot, or a journalled trial whose result is not submitted; a dispatch journal that does not verify or does not follow planned_slots in order (out-of-order or extra slots); a dispatched trial record of this manifest under run_identity.trial_base_dir that is not in the journal, a trial directory there without a readable record; more than one judging of a trial, i.e. a trial's judge log that is not exactly the one judging its result carries (a second judging, a judge log without a judging result, an edited or removed judge log); a critic request id, critic message id, judge request id or judge message id that is not in the adapter's form or that occurs twice in the suite; expectations loaded without the composition check; a pre-dispatch manifest or profile that does not verify or does not pin exactly these expectations, materials, case digests and case order
suite_outcome.not_judged: no fail and not incomplete, and any semantic item is not_judged (a judge answer of undetermined, a judge answer without the judge provider's reported identity, or a profile without established judge separation)
suite_outcome.one_judging_per_trial: every trial is judged exactly once (judge.one_judging_per_trial): checked by verify_trial (the exclusive judge log) and verify_suite (the re-read judge logs), and after the verdict by the post-verdict audit: the judge provider's judge-model requests in the run window equal the logged judge request ids, in both directions

acceptance.suite_record: conforms to suite_record.schema.json (q01-release-suite-verdict-v6): the critic configuration digest, the pre-dispatch manifest sha256, the attempt number with prior verdicts, every prior attempt's sealed set sha256 and a digest of the prior-attempt list, the dispatch journal head, the manifest's commit reference, the profile sha256, judge separation (from the profile), the V3 status (always unverified under this design, derived by the verifier, never from the caller), critic_transport_identity and judge_transport_identity (provider_reported or not_attested, from the verified results), run_stopped (from the journal), judge_logs (each submitted trial's judge-log lines_sha256, audit 6 Y1) and provider_ids_sha256 with provider_id_count (the sorted provider ids, audit 6 Y2); built only from an issued suite result and the same re-checked run and journal
acceptance.what_a_pass_confers: status scoped_pass for exactly this critic configuration digest. This design cannot verify V3 (no generation path), so a scoped pass is NOT a critic qualification and approves no design; the product gate reads only q01-release-v7 records, recomputes record_sha256 and refuses a mismatch, refuses (does not cap) a record that is not schema-valid (a V3 status other than unverified, a sealed set listed among its prior attempts' sets, a pass without a journal head or commit reference, a pass whose critic or judge transport identity is not provider_reported, a pass of a stopped run, a pass without a judge-log digest for every trial or without its provider ids), and caps every valid q01-release-v7 pass at scoped_pass. Qualification is reachable only from a design declared able to verify V3 in the gate's V3_VERIFYING_DESIGN_IDS, which is empty; the gate has no test hook (tests replace V3_VERIFYING_DESIGN_IDS for the duration of one test). The gate checks a record's shape and self-consistency only: it cannot tell a record built by build_suite_record from one assembled by hand with the same fields (see open).
acceptance.open: criticism verdicts do not yet carry the critic configuration digest that produced them, so design approval cannot yet bind the qualification's digest to the verdict's critic; this is required before any V3-verifying design is admitted
acceptance.post_verdict: Every pass and any suspicious result is audited after the verdict (verification.md section 4), including every item of post_verdict_audit. A verifier or harness defect found after the verdict voids it to incomplete; it never upgrades a fail.
post_verdict_audit: the manifest sha256 was committed (the commit id in manifest_commit_ref contains it) or externally timestamped before the first ledger event of the first journalled trial
the dispatch journal at run_identity.dispatch_journal.path is the only journal for this manifest and its head equals the suite record's dispatch_journal_head

no trial of this manifest exists outside the journal: every trial directory under run_identity.trial_base_dir is journalled (checked by verify_suite) and no directory was removed from it (the operator's filesystem and backup history)

two-way reconciliation of every provider id with the provider's own records (audit 6, Y2), for the account, the critic model and the judge model and the run's time window: (a) each logged critic request id, critic message id and judge request id is distinct (also checked by verify_suite) and its provider record matches the call's model, time window and token usage; AND (b) the provider's requests for that account, those models and that window are exactly the logged ids: no unlogged request exists (no retry, re-ask, peek or second judging)

one judging per trial (audit 6, Y1): every trial's judge log holds exactly one judging (re-read by verify_suite), and the judge provider's judge-model requests in the run window equal the logged judge request ids in both directions, so a judge log that was removed and judged again, or a judge wrapper that re-asked the provider, is detected
no listed prior attempt, and no other known attempt or manifest of this configuration digest, used this sealed set or any of its cases

reporting: per case and boundary class: passes, misses (a required defect not found), false rejections (a valid candidate or alternative rejected), abstentions, and not_judged items, each with its real denominator
judge-versus-expectation disagreements per item, labelled judge_disagreement (never a joint error)
same-item critic misses and false rejections; V3 joint-error metrics are not computed because this design has no generation path
cluster counts (cases sharing materials count as one cluster)
every invalid trial with its cause, calls, tokens, spend and wall time
attempt k and all prior verdicts for this configuration
the dispatch journal (every entry, in order) and its head
the provider-reported served model, request id and message id of every critic call and judge answer, the judge logs with their digests, and the two-way reconciliation of the ids
the stop entry of the dispatch journal, if any
claims_if_passed: Attempt k of this exact critic configuration met the frozen acceptance rule on this sealed set, in 3 repetitions per case, with every dispatched trial journalled and submitted and each trial judged once (prior attempts and verdicts listed).

Every critic call recorded, as the pinned harness and product adapter parsed it, the configured model as served and a provider request id and message id in the adapter's forms, all distinct across the suite; every semantic item was judged once by the configured judge model, as reported, with its raw response kept. Code checks only the form, the distinctness and the logs; that each id is a real provider request of that model, and that the provider received no unlogged request, rests on the two-way reconciliation with the provider's records (post_verdict_audit), not on code.
V3 (error independence) remains unmet and cannot be met under this design: no critic qualification and no design approval follow from a scoped pass.
never_claimed: an error rate, false-rejection rate or missed-defect rate beyond the observed counts (Task.md open decision on quantitative qualification remains unmet)
generalization to other tasks or materials
that a provider-reported identity proves which weights served a call (it is what the provider's response said)
open: criticism verdicts do not carry the critic configuration digest (acceptance.open)

the journal, trial directories, trial records, ledgers and judge log live on the operator's disk: the hash chain, the per-call ledger binding, the trial base directory scan and the post-verdict audit detect edits made through the harness path and a restored journal backup while the failed trial's directory remains, not a determined operator who rewrites or deletes every file (for example removes the failed trial's directory as well as restoring the journal)
the commit-before-first-dispatch order is an audit item, not checked by code

provider attestation is what the pinned product adapter parsed from the HTTP response it received, and code checks only the form and distinctness of the ids: in-process constructed replies (a ProviderReply or AttestedJudgement built by Python code with fresh, well-formed, distinct ids), a fake provider server or an intercepting proxy pass the harness and verifier. They are caught only by the external two-way reconciliation of the logged ids with the provider's records (post_verdict_audit), which is not automated

the declared critic transport is what the Claude rig reports about how it was built; an in-process caller can attach any declaration to a turn, so a mismatch between declaration and reality is caught only by the provider reconciliation

one judging per trial is enforced on the operator's disk: an operator who deletes a trial's judge log and judges again leaves a consistent log; the first judging's judge-model requests are then unlogged provider requests, detected only by the two-way reconciliation (post_verdict_audit)

edited or renamed spent cases pass the spent-set digest and id comparisons; excluding them relies on must_be_new and human review (author, reviewer, sealing attestations) and on the post-verdict audit item on other attempts (pre_dispatch.spent_sets)
the served model is compared exactly with critic_configuration.model; a configuration must pin the exact model string the provider reports (provider alias-to-snapshot resolution is not modelled)
max_tokens is not observable by the transport and is recorded as unchecked
no attested human-reviewer judge path exists: a human reviewer's answers leave semantic items not_judged under this design
the judge-family check compares declared names with a provider/family alias table and only guards against accidental self-judging

second-manifest cherry-picking (audit 5, item 2): nothing in code enumerates every manifest written for one critic configuration digest, so an operator can write a second manifest for the same sealed set as attempt 1 with no prior attempts and a fresh journal and trial base directory; each manifest's own checks pass. Detection is organizational: every manifest is externally anchored (committed or timestamped) before dispatch, and the post-verdict audit checks that no other known attempt or manifest of the configuration digest used the set

hand-built record provenance (audit 5, item 4): the product gate checks a suite record's schema, self-consistency and record_sha256 only; a record assembled by hand with consistent fields reaches scoped_pass. Provenance rests on external anchoring (the committed manifest, the journal, the trial records and ledgers) and the post-verdict audit, not on the gate
the T077 dispatcher that enforces usd_hard_stop and journals the stop entry does not exist yet; no release run executes until it is written, reviewed and pinned in a later version
